title: Illinois's 17th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Illinois's 17th Congressional District covers northwestern and central Illinois, including Rockford, the Quad Cities area, Peoria, and surrounding rural communities. Incumbent Democratic Representative Eric Sorensen, a former television meteorologist first elected in 2022, is seeking a third term. The Republican nominee is Dillan Vancil, a small business owner and former train engineer who won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 57.2% of the vote. The district is considered competitive and has flipped between parties in recent cycles, with Sorensen emphasizing bipartisan cooperation and Vancil focusing on conservative economic and energy policies.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found for this race at the time of research.

candidates.name: Eric Sorensen
candidates.summary: Eric Sorensen is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Illinois's 17th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. Before Congress, he worked as a local TV meteorologist for over two decades in Rockford and the Quad Cities. He serves on the House Agriculture Committee and the House Armed Services Committee, and was the first openly LGBTQ+ person elected to Congress from Illinois.

candidates.name: Dillan Vancil
candidates.summary: Dillan Vancil is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 17th Congressional District, having won the March 17, 2026 primary with 57.2% of the vote. He is a small business owner who operates Dame Fine Coffee, a drive-through coffee chain with six locations in Illinois and one in Iowa. Vancil also served as Vice President of the West Central School Board and previously worked for a decade as a train engineer and as State Legislative Director for the SMART-TD union.

forecast.rationale: No independent public polling exists for this race, severely limiting quantitative confidence. The district is described as competitive and has flipped between parties in recent cycles, indicating a closely divided electorate without a strong built-in partisan lean. Incumbent Eric Sorensen has won two consecutive terms in this swing district (2022 and 2024), providing Democrats a modest structural edge through incumbency, name recognition from his two-decade career as a local TV meteorologist, and committee assignments. Republican nominee Dillan Vancil is a credible challenger with a competitive primary win (57.2%) and local leadership experience, which gives the GOP a realistic pathway in a favorable national environment. However, sparse candidate-level data, no polling, and the district's swing character make any forecast highly uncertain. The rating reflects a narrow Democratic advantage based on incumbency in a competitive seat, but the confidence is low due to the absence of polling and limited information on district-specific dynamics in the current cycle.
